messages:
jordan: Quick intake — Customer: AcmePay. Problem: they need per-tenant controls for graceful degradation when models or regions become constrained. They want a 'landing pad' config that defines fallback routing, quality thresholds, and rollout guardrails so their app doesn't break or cost explode when we scale down higher-tier variants.

jordan: Goals:
- Provide tenant-scoped routing/fallback policy (which model variants to try, in what order)
- Per-tenant min-quality thresholds that can trigger automatic rollback or alerting
- Safe rollout UI/flag + metrics to validate before full enablement

jordan: Non-goals:
- We will NOT ship a per-tenant model training or fine-tuning pipeline (out of scope)
- We won't change core latency SLOs for global traffic; landing pad should respect existing SLOs unless tenant explicitly relaxes them

maya: couple clarifying q's: is the landing pad purely routing (model selection/region) or do they want per-tenant prompt rewriting/covers?

jordan: mainly routing + fallback thresholds. They said optional prompt templates later, but initial ask is about safe fallback ordering and an acceptance gate.

srinivas: infra constraints to flag:
- Routing table needs to be consistently readable by inference proxies (low-latency path).
- Per-tenant config size must be tiny; prefer references to shared strategy records instead of full payloads on each request.
- KV cache invalidation on rollout changes is tricky (we'll need TTLs or version keys).

liz: from CS: must have audit trail (who toggled what), easy rollback, and a UI toggle visible to customer success. Also customers want a 'safety buffer'—a short grace period before fallback becomes active so they can monitor.

kai: success metrics I propose we track by tenant during canary:
- %requests hitting fallback vs baseline
- latency p95 change after fallback applied
- quality regression rate measured by eval prompt set (we can run ~1000 evals pre/post)
- cost delta per 1k requests

maya: implementation sketch: store a tenantLandingPad record in tenant-configs with small fields: fallbackFlowRef (points to a shared flow object), minQualityScore (0-100), graceSeconds, rolloutFlag. Proxy reads landingPadRef and resolves shared flow -> model order. Example snippet:```json
{"landingPadRef": "shared:lp-v1", "minQuality": 85, "graceSeconds": 300, "rolloutFlag": "feat/tenant-lp/acmepay"}```
Acceptance criteria (engineering):
- Proxy can resolve a landingPadRef in <2ms for 99th pct of lookups
- Changing rolloutFlag flips behavior within 1 minute (or documented TTL)
- If model order exhausted, fallback to org-global default and emit event with tenant id

jordan: product acceptance criteria:
- Customer can author landing pad via Console or API and validate via a dry-run endpoint
- Can set minQuality; when breach occurs, either auto-rollback or open ticket depending on tenant policy
- UI shows a timeline of when landing pad was active + triggered events

srinivas: rollout plan idea: feature-flagged canary -> staged ramp (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic halt if eval quality delta > X or latency p95 increase > Y. Flag backend uses our existing metering and gating infra.

liz: ops ask: add an opt-in consent checkbox for customers who want us to auto-rollback on quality breach. Some legal/regulators want explicit opt-in for automatic behavior.

kai: for gating thresholds we should define concrete numbers now so devs can wire alerts:
- quality regression > 3% absolute on evaluation set -> halt
- latency p95 increase > 50ms -> pause ramp
- cost increase > 20% per 1k tokens -> alert but not auto-halt

maya: edge cases / open questions:
- tenant config conflicts when multiple updates arrive; need last-writer-wins or version pinning? recommend version pins with human override.
- what happens for short-lived tenants with tiny request volume (no eval signals)? fallback to conservative defaults.

jordan: next steps:
1) Maya & Srinivas draft a short RFC with config schema, proxy resolution path, and rollout recipe (due EOD Fri).
2) Kai to prepare a 1k-sample eval set for AcmePay and baseline metrics (due Tue).
3) Liz to document support playbook and consent text (due Tue).

jordan: metrics dashboard asks: can we show tenant-level KPIs for the canary? kai/srinivas?

kai: yes, we can add tenant filters to the existing rollout dashboard; need tags from proxy events (landingPadRef + tenant_id). I'll prototype queries this week.

srinivas: noted. I'll add event payloads: {tenant_id, landing_pad_ref, resolved_models, fallback_reason, latency_ms} (we'll keep as small JSON) and a short retention policy to avoid blowup.

liz: :thumbsup: from CS. Also looping in sales to set expectations with AcmePay.

jordan: thanks all — I'll post RFC link here when ready. Quick ack if you saw action items.

maya: ack

kai: ack

srinivas: ack

liz: ack
